title: Stage A1.2 - Past Tenses, Present Perfect, & Daily Life
description: Talk about your past experiences, daily routines, and handle everyday situations like shopping, dining, and describing the weather.

grammar.title: Preterite (Pretérito Indefinido) - Regular Verbs
grammar.content:
The preterite tense is used to talk about completed actions in the past with a clear beginning or end. Think of it as the 'storytelling' tense - you're telling someone what happened.

For regular -AR verbs (like hablar), the endings are:
- yo: -é
- tú: -aste
- él/ella/usted: -ó
- nosotros: -amos
- vosotros: -asteis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -aron

For regular -ER/-IR verbs (like comer, vivir), the endings are:
- yo: -í
- tú: -iste
- él/ella/usted: -ió
- nosotros: -imos
- vosotros: -isteis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -ieron
examples: Ayer hablé con mi amigo. (Yesterday I talked with my friend.)
Ellos comieron pizza anoche. (They ate pizza last night.)
Nosotros vivimos en Madrid dos años. (We lived in Madrid for two years.)
grammar.aid_note: Watch out: 'nosotros' form looks the same for -AR preterite and present! Context tells you which: 'hablamos' in present = we speak; 'hablamos' in preterite = we spoke. Look for time words like 'ayer' (yesterday), 'la semana pasada' (last week).

grammar.title: Preterite - High-Frequency Irregular Verbs (ESTAR, IR, HACER, TENER, DECIR)
grammar.content:
These five verbs share the same irregular stem in the preterite: tuv-, estuv-, hic-, dij-, and for IR it's fui/fuiste... (different pattern). They also all drop the accent on nosotros.

The shared endings (for ESTAR, IR, HACER, TENER, DECIR) are:
- yo: -e
- tú: -iste
- él/ella/usted: -o
- nosotros: -imos (no accent)
- vosotros: -isteis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -ieron
examples: Ayer estuve en el parque. (Yesterday I was at the park.)
El año pasado fui a Italia. (Last year I went to Italy.)
Ella hizo la cena. (She made dinner.)
Tuvimos un buen día. (We had a good day.)
Juan dijo la verdad. (Juan told the truth.)
grammar.aid_note: IR (to go) and ESTAR (to be) have the SAME preterite forms. Context determines meaning: 'Ayer fui al cine' (I went to the cinema) vs 'Ayer estuve en el cine' (I was at the cinema). Both are correct but slightly different meanings.

grammar.title: Present Perfect (Pretérito Perfecto)
grammar.content:
The present perfect combines 'haber' (to have) in the present + a past participle. It's used for recent past actions or experiences that have relevance to the present. In Spain, it's very common for 'today' or 'this week.'

Conjugation of HABER (present): yo he, tú has, él/ella/usted ha, nosotros hemos, vosotros habéis, ellos/ellas/ustedes han.

Past participles:
- -AR verbs: replace -ar with -ado (hablar -> hablado)
- -ER verbs: replace -er with -ido (comer -> comido)
- -IR verbs: replace -ir with -ido (vivir -> vivido)

Irregular past participles: hacer -> hecho, decir -> dicho, escribir -> escrito, ver -> visto, abrir -> abierto, romper -> roto, volver -> vuelto, cubrir -> cubierto.
examples: Hoy he desayunado tarde. (Today I had breakfast late.)
Ya he visto esa película. (I've already seen that movie.)
¿Has escrito la carta? (Have you written the letter?)
Nosotros hemos vivido aquí siempre. (We have always lived here.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian uses a similar structure with 'a avut' (has had) + participle. In Spanish, HABER is ALWAYS the helper - never use ESTAR. 'He comido' (I have eaten) NOT 'Estoy comido'.

grammar.title: Demonstrative Adjectives (este, ese, aquel)
grammar.content:
Spanish has three degrees of distance for 'this/that/those':

Near the speaker (this/these): este/esta/estos/estas
Near the listener (that/those): ese/esos esa/esas
Far from both (that/those over there): aquel/aquella/aquellos/aquellas

They must agree in gender and number with the noun they describe. There are also neuter forms (esto, eso, aquello) used for abstract concepts or when you don't know the gender.
examples: Esta casa es bonita. (This house is pretty.)
Ese libro es mío. (That book is mine.)
Aquellos montañas son hermosas. (Those mountains over there are beautiful.)
Quiero eso. (I want that.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian has a similar system: 'acest' (near speaker), 'acel' (distant), 'acesta' (near listener). Spanish is simpler with just 3 levels instead of Romanian's 4.

grammar.title: Possessive Adjectives (mi, tu, su, nuestro...)
grammar.content:
Possessive adjectives show ownership and agree in NUMBER (singular/plural) with the noun they modify, not with the owner.

Short forms (before the noun):
- mi(s) = my
- tu(s) = your (informal)
- su(s) = his/her/their/your formal
- nuestro/a(s) = our
- vuestro/a(s) = your (plural, Spain informal)

Note: 'su' can mean many things! Context and prepositional phrases (de mí, de ti, de él) clarify.
examples: Mi casa es grande. (My house is big.)
¿Dónde están tus llaves? (Where are your keys?)
Su padre es doctor. (His/her father is a doctor.)
Nuestro gato se llama Luna. (Our cat is named Luna.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian has a very similar system: 'al meu/al tău/al său/al nostru' but uses different forms. Spanish 'mi/tu/su' are simpler - no gender agreement needed for the short forms (except nuestro/vuestro).

grammar.title: Time Expressions & Basic Adverbs
grammar.content:
These time words help you talk about when things happened. They're essential for the preterite tense.

Key time expressions:
- ayer = yesterday
- anteayer = the day before yesterday
- la semana pasada = last week
- el mes pasado = last month
- el año pasado = last year
- hace + time = ago (hace dos días = two days ago)
- hace poco = recently, a short while ago
- hoy = today
- mañana = tomorrow
- ahora = now
- luego = later
- después = after, then

Key adverbs:
- siempre = always
- nunca/nuncay = never
- a veces = sometimes
- siempre = always
- ya = already
- todavía = still, yet
- todavía no = not yet
examples: Ayer por la noche no pude dormir. (Last night I couldn't sleep.)
Hace una semana que no la veo. (It's been a week since I saw her.)
Siempre desayuno café con leche. (I always have coffee with milk for breakfast.)
grammar.aid_note: 'Hace' is the 3rd person of 'hacer' (to do/make) but here it means 'ago.' 'Hace dos años' literally means 'it makes two years.' Also used for duration: 'Vivo aquí hace dos años' (I've been living here for two years).

pronunciation.title: Question Words (Palabras Interrogativas)
pronunciation.content:
Spanish uses question words to ask questions. They always have an accent mark, and in written Spanish, questions are enclosed between ¿ and ?.

The main question words:
- ¿Qué? = What?
- ¿Quién? = Who?
- ¿Cuánto(a)? = How much/many?
- ¿Dónde? = Where?
- ¿Cuándo? = When?
- ¿Por qué? = Why?
- ¿Cómo? = How?
- ¿Cuál(es)? = Which?

Note: 'Qué' (with accent) means 'what.' 'Que' (no accent) means 'that.' This is a common mistake!
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian has similar question words: 'ce' (what), 'cine' (who), 'unde' (where), 'când' (when), 'de ce' (why), 'cum' (how). Spanish adds 'cuánto' for quantities and 'cuál' for choices.

pronunciation.title: Intonation in Questions
pronunciation.content:
Spanish questions have a characteristic rising-falling intonation pattern. When you speak a question, your voice typically rises at the beginning and falls at the end.

Statements vs Questions (same words, different intonation):
- Él come pan. (He eats bread.) - flat tone
- ¿Él come pan? (Does he eat bread?) - rising then falling

Yes/No questions and question-word questions both use intonation, but question-word questions have the pitch starting lower on the question word and rising before the end.

In writing, the accent mark on question words is mandatory: ¿Qué, ¿Quién, ¿Dónde, etc.
pronunciation.aid_note: Unlike Romanian which often changes word order for questions, Spanish keeps the same word order and just uses intonation + ¿? marks. This makes it easier for Romanian speakers!

pronunciation.title: The Rolled R vs Single R
pronunciation.content:
Spanish has a single tap /r/ and a rolled trill /rr/. Understanding the difference is key to being understood.

Single /r/ (tap - one quick flash of the tongue):
- Between vowels: caro (expensive), perro (dog)
- At the start of a word: rojo (red), ramo (bunch)
- After consonants: azul (blue)

Double /rr/ or R at the start of a word (trill - multiple rapid flashes):
- Between vowels: perro (dog), cerveza (beer)
- At the start: rojo (red), Romeo

Tip: The rolled R requires airflow - place your tongue tip behind your upper teeth and blow air. It's like the sound a motor makes.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian also has a single 'r' sound that's similar to the Spanish tap. The rolled trill is an extra skill - practice with words like 'perro' (dog) vs 'pero' (but).

exercises.question: What is the preterite form of 'hablar' for 'yo'?
exercises.explanation: 'Hablé' is the yo form of hablar in the preterite. The -é ending marks first-person singular preterite for -AR verbs.

exercises.question: Which time expression means 'yesterday' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Ayer' means yesterday. 'Mañana' is tomorrow, 'hoy' is today, 'anteayer' is the day before yesterday.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Nosotros ____ (comer) pizza anoche.' (We ate pizza last night.)
exercises.explanation: 'Comimos' is the nosotros form of comer in the preterite. -IR ending for -ER verb nosotros.

exercises.question: What does 'hace calor' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Hace calor' means 'It's hot' (literally: 'it makes heat'). For cold: 'hace frío'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ella ____ (decir) la verdad ayer.' (She told the truth yesterday.)
exercises.explanation: 'Dijo' is the irregular preterite of decir for él/ella/usted. The stem changes to dij-.

exercises.question: Match each Spanish daily routine verb with its English meaning:
exercises.explanation: These reflexive and regular verbs are key for describing your daily routine.

exercises.question: What is the correct demonstrative for 'this book (near me)?'
exercises.explanation: 'Este libro' means 'this book' (near the speaker). 'Este' is masculine singular, matching 'libro'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Hoy yo ____ (hacer) la tarea.' (Today I did the homework.)
exercises.explanation: 'Hice' is the irregular preterite of hacer for yo. The stem changes to hic-.

exercises.question: What is the present perfect of 'yo + hablar'?
exercises.explanation: 'He hablado' is the present perfect: yo form of haber (he) + past participle (hablado).

exercises.question: Complete: 'Mis ____ (key) están en la mesa.' (My keys are on the table.)
exercises.explanation: 'Llaves' is the plural of llave (key). 'Mis' matches the plural - 'mi' would be singular.

exercises.question: What does 'nunca' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Nunca' means never. Note: 'Siempre' = always, 'A veces' = sometimes, 'Ya' = already.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ayer ____ (estar) en el supermercado.' (Yesterday I was at the supermarket.)
exercises.explanation: 'Estuve' is the irregular preterite of estar for yo. The stem changes to estuv-.

exercises.question: Which verb means 'to go to bed' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Irse a la cama' means 'to go to bed.' 'Dormir' means 'to sleep' (the state, not the action of going to bed).

exercises.question: Match the days of the week:
exercises.explanation: All days of the week are masculine in Spanish and are preceded by 'el' (el lunes, el martes, etc.).

exercises.question: What is the preterite of 'tener' for 'él/ella'?
exercises.explanation: 'Tuvo' is the correct preterite form. Note the accent on the o - it follows the rule for words ending in a vowel (stress on 2nd-to-last by default).

exercises.question: Complete: '¿____ (haber) ____ (you) comido?' (Have you eaten?)
exercises.explanation: '¿Has comido?' is the present perfect: tú form of haber (has) + past participle (comido).

exercises.question: What does 'hace frío' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Hace frío' means 'It's cold' (literally: 'it makes cold'). 'Hace calor' = it's hot.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Yo ____ (ir) al mercado la semana pasada.' (I went to the market last week.)
exercises.explanation: 'Fui' is the irregular preterite of ir for yo. IR and ESTAR share the same preterite conjugations.

exercises.question: Match the food vocabulary:
exercises.explanation: These are common food items you'll encounter at breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

exercises.question: What is the correct demonstrative for 'those mountains (far from both of us)?'
exercises.explanation: 'Aquellas montañas' uses the far-distance demonstrative (aquel) in feminine plural form, matching 'montañas.'

exercises.question: Complete: 'Nosotros ____ (vivir) en España hace cinco años.' (We have lived in Spain for five years.)
exercises.explanation: Wait - this uses 'hace' + duration for 'for.' 'Nosotros vivimos en España hace cinco años' uses the preterite of vivir. But for present perfect of living: 'Hemos vivido.' For 'hace' (duration marker): 'Hace cinco años que vivimos aquí.' The answer depends on sentence structure.

exercises.question: What is the question word for 'where' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: '¿Dónde?' means 'Where?' It always has an accent mark. Written questions use ¿dónde...?'

exercises.question: Complete: '¿Cuánto ____ (costar) esto?' (How much does this cost?)
exercises.explanation: 'Cuesta' is the él/ella/usted form of costar. In questions, you use the third person: '¿Cuánto cuesta?'

exercises.question: What is the irregular past participle of 'hacer'?
exercises.explanation: 'Hecho' is the irregular past participle of hacer. Used in present perfect: 'He hecho' (I have done).
exercises.aid_note: Common irregular participles: hacer->hecho, decir->dicho, escribir->escrito, ver->visto, abrir->abierto.

exercises.question: Match the weather expressions:
exercises.explanation: Weather expressions are essential for small talk and planning daily activities in Spanish.

exercises.question: Complete the preterite tense conjugation table for HACER:
exercises.explanation: Hacer is irregular in the preterite (hic- stem). This is one of the most common verbs in Spanish.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the correct present perfect?
exercises.explanation: 'He comido' is correct: yo form of haber (he) + past participle (comido). Has = tú, ha = él/ella, hemos = nosotros.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Tú ____ (dormir) ocho horas anoche.' (You slept eight hours last night.)
exercises.explanation: 'Dormiste' is the tú form of dormir in the preterite. Note: dormir has a stem change (o->ue) in present but NOT in preterite yo/nosotros.

exercises.question: What does 'todavía no' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Todavía no' means 'not yet.' 'Todavía sí' means 'still yes.' 'Ya' means 'already.'

exercises.question: Complete: 'Hace dos días yo ____ (llegar) a Madrid.' (I arrived in Madrid two days ago.)
exercises.explanation: 'Llegué' is the yo form of llegar in the preterite. -AR verbs get -é for yo preterite.

exercises.question: Which of these is a reflexive verb for daily routine?
exercises.explanation: 'Despertarse' (to wake up) is reflexive - the action reflects back on the subject: yo me despierto.
